video_title: Head Coach Jordan Ott Postgame Media Availability | 11-2-26

quotes.speaker: Jordan Ott
quotes.summary_phrase: Jordan Ott on Phoenix's fourth-quarter execution and turnovers
quotes.excerpt: Got to get a shot up, got to execute a little better.
quotes.quote: In the fourth, it got choppy in the second half. 27 free throws I think they had in the second half, and then we had seven turnovers there in the fourth. Got to get a shot up, got to execute a little better. We will take a look, get back to the practice floor.
quotes.social_post: Jordan Ott points to turnovers and free throw disparity as the main culprits in the Suns fourth quarter struggles. He says the team needs to execute better and get shots up down the stretch.

structured.context: Head coach Jordan Ott discusses the team's fourth-quarter execution and turnovers following a loss.

quotes.speaker: Jordan Ott
quotes.summary_phrase: Jordan Ott provides injury update on player's calf
quotes.excerpt: It is just his right calf.
quotes.quote: I am not sure exactly. I think it was opposite of our bench, whether he was going towards the rim for some reason, whether he was tagging or whatever, but yeah, it is just his right calf.
quotes.social_post: Jordan Ott provides an update on the injury situation for his player, confirming it is a right calf issue but noting he is not yet sure of the full extent of the injury.

structured.context: Jordan Ott provides an update on a player's right calf injury sustained during the game.

quotes.speaker: Jordan Ott
quotes.summary_phrase: Jordan Ott on the team's lack of preseason chemistry
quotes.excerpt: This feels like the first time it was that tight down the stretch.
quotes.quote: It is a newer group. This feels like the first time it was that tight down the stretch. I think those are some good reps to get. That is where you miss a little bit of the preseason or how we started the season. Credit to them, they are a good defensive team, especially when they are locked in in that fourth quarter.
quotes.social_post: Jordan Ott believes the Suns are still working through chemistry issues as a newer group, noting that tight games like tonight are good reps for a team that missed out on preseason time together.

structured.context: Jordan Ott reflects on the team's lack of chemistry and experience in close games due to the short preseason.

quotes.speaker: Jordan Ott
quotes.summary_phrase: Jordan Ott on team composure during high-stakes moments
quotes.excerpt: We talked about staying in it for 48 minutes, having the mental resilience to stay in it.
quotes.quote: Overall, I think they closed the gap there right before the half. We talked about staying in it for 48 minutes, having the mental resilience to stay in it, especially with this team that can get hot at any second. And then even into the fourth, the way it played out, we hung in there on the road with a newer group. Those things are definitely, we need to put a full 48 together.
quotes.social_post: Jordan Ott emphasizes the need for mental resilience and playing a full 48 minutes, praising his team for hanging in there on the road despite the late game pressure.

structured.context: Jordan Ott comments on the team's mental resilience and the need to play a full 48 minutes.

quotes.speaker: Jordan Ott
quotes.summary_phrase: Jordan Ott on inconsistent officiating and foul calls
quotes.excerpt: It is just frustrating with the contact of a bump on a cross screen versus driving downhill.
quotes.quote: It is just frustrating with the contact of a bump on a cross screen versus driving downhill appears to be different disruption. When you are just going to take a cut to get a catch versus downhill, we are top ten in drives, we are bottom five in free throws. So some of that, we definitely have to clean up, fouling the jump shooters, but trying to figure out what exactly pressure you can apply and which pressure puts you in a spot to where free throws are rewarded.
quotes.social_post: Jordan Ott expresses frustration with officiating, noting the Suns are top ten in drives but bottom five in free throws. He says the team is trying to figure out what kind of defensive pressure they can apply without being penalized.

structured.context: Jordan Ott expresses frustration regarding inconsistent officiating and the disparity in free throw attempts.

quotes.speaker: Jordan Ott
quotes.summary_phrase: Jordan Ott on Devin's rhythm and defensive energy
quotes.excerpt: When you enjoy and feel the energy from defense, how easily offense flows.
quotes.quote: Dwayne and I are going to continue to talk about our defense. It is amazing when you enjoy and feel the energy from defense, how easily offense flows. I thought Jaylen made a lot of great passes tonight. They were putting two on the basketball on book, he hit the roller or he hit the pull behind, so I thought there was a lot of good possessions again offensively. It is the defense that we are going to continue to try to figure out.
quotes.social_post: Jordan Ott says the Suns offense flows better when the team prioritizes defensive energy. He praised Jaylen for making great passes out of double teams on Devin.

structured.context: Jordan Ott discusses defensive energy and the offensive contributions of Jaylen and Devin Booker.

quotes.speaker: Jordan Ott
quotes.summary_phrase: Jordan Ott on Devin's fourth-quarter foul trouble
quotes.excerpt: He had to sit out, he is in foul trouble.
quotes.quote: He had to sit out, he is in foul trouble for a large part of that. He got his fifth, had to come to the bench, that breaks your rhythm. You are trying to play a competitive night of basketball and then you have to come to the bench because you are in foul trouble.
quotes.social_post: Jordan Ott notes that Devin being in foul trouble for a large part of the game disrupted the team rhythm, making it difficult to play a competitive game.

structured.context: Jordan Ott explains how foul trouble disrupted Devin Booker's rhythm during the fourth quarter.
